title: Signature Breadth-First Source Crawl — Core Method
description: Signature original by Justin Addam Higgins. Recursive discovery starts from seed sources and expands outward in breadth-first order, so the nearest and most relevant sources are found before the crawl drifts far afield. A visited set guarantees each source is processed once even when the source graph has cycles. Each newly discovered source is enqueued with its discovery depth, which keeps the expansion orderly and explainable. This is the same discipline web crawlers use to cover huge graphs without drowning in repeats. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method. title: Signature Citation Chasing — Core Method
description: Signature original by Justin Addam Higgins. Every record cites other records, and those citations are a map to sources the searcher did not know existed. Citation chasing extracts references from each discovered record, resolves them to source locations, and adds the new sources to the discovery frontier. Because citations reflect what authors actually relied on, this finds high-value sources that keyword search often misses. Academic literature search has worked this way for decades, forward and backward through citation graphs. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method. Lineage: Signature-line counterpart of the public method of the same name, filed as a Signature original in the Signature archive.
demo:
RECORDS = {"r1": ["r2", "r3"], "r2": ["r3", "r4"], "r3": [], "r4": ["r1"]}
frontier, seen = ["r1"], set()
while frontier:
    r = frontier.pop(0)
    if r in seen: continue
    seen.add(r)
    print("examined", r, "-> cites", RECORDS[r])
    frontier.extend(c for c in RECORDS[r] if c not in seen)
print("discovered records:", sorted(seen))

title: Signature Frontier Prioritization — Core Method
description: Signature original by Justin Addam Higgins. Not all undiscovered sources deserve equal attention, so the discovery frontier is a priority queue scored by expected value: citation count, topical overlap with the mission, freshness, and source reputation. High-scoring candidates are explored first, which means the engine finds the best sources early even if it never finishes the crawl. Scores are updated as new evidence arrives, so the frontier adapts instead of following a fixed order. This is best-first search applied to the problem of where to look next. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method. Lineage: Signature-line counterpart of the public method of the same name, filed as a Signature original in the Signature archive.
demo:
import heapq
frontier = []
def push(name, cites, overlap):
    heapq.heappush(frontier, (-(cites * 2 + overlap * 10), name))
push("s1", 3, 0.9); push("s2", 10, 0.2); push("s3", 1, 0.8)
while frontier:
    neg, name = heapq.heappop(frontier)
    print("explore", name, "priority=%.1f" % -neg)

title: Signature Depth-Limited Recursion — Core Method
description: Signature original by Justin Addam Higgins. Unbounded recursion over a densely linked archive can explode, so the engine carries a depth budget: each hop away from the seed costs one unit, and expansion stops when the budget runs out. The visited set from the crawl combines with the depth cap to guarantee termination on any graph, cyclic or not. Depth also serves as a relevance signal — sources found in fewer hops are usually more pertinent. Iterative deepening can then re-run with larger budgets when the first pass comes up short. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method. title: Signature Source Graph Expansion — Core Method
description: Signature original by Justin Addam Higgins. As discovery proceeds, the engine builds an explicit graph of what it found: nodes for sources, edges for how each was discovered, weights for the strength of the connection. This graph becomes a durable map of the archive neighborhood that later missions can reuse instead of rediscovering. Expansion rules decide which edges to follow — co-citation, shared authorship, shared topics — and each rule is logged so the map explains itself. Over many missions the graph compounds into genuine knowledge of the archive's structure. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method. Lineage: Signature-line counterpart of the public method of the same name, filed as a Signature original in the Signature archive.
